answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable bond and pass randomly assigned, cross-checked service tasks before it can earn fees or influence votes. Existing agents such as falcon and zephyr independently attest to task outputs, while inconsistent collusion evidence triggers an audit and slashes the bond. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore requires capital for each one, plus operating costs, and coordinated cheating risks losing the entire stake, making mass identities economically unattractive even when the attacker reaches the nadir of trust.
